title: High IV is not enough: the edge needs low realized volatility
summary: Selling covered calls just because implied volatility is high is half the story. If you sell at 60% IV while the stock moves at 70% annualized, there is no edge. If you sell at 60% IV while the stock moves only 25%, you are paid far more than the stock delivers. That gap is the volatility risk premium.

steps.caption: A volatile stock with option IV near 60%.
Implied volatility near 60%: the premium looks rich.
Realized (historical) volatility near 25%: the stock moves much less than priced.
The gap of about 35 points is the volatility risk premium. That is where the edge lives.
Raise base RV to 70%: now RV exceeds IV, and the same 60% IV call has no edge.

takeaways: High IV alone does not make a good covered call.
60% IV against 70% realized volatility: no edge.
60% IV against 25% realized volatility: a large edge.
IV minus realized volatility is the volatility risk premium.
caveats: The speaker's metric behind the bio link is promotional and not verified here.
